findings.detail: For an initialized checkout named -vendor containing an untracked symlink new-link, recursive collection emits -vendor/new-link. The prescribed discovery snippet passes that relative path directly to readlink, which interprets it as options. The assignment fails and || exit terminates discovery before producing the required link annotation. The unsafe operand handling predates this change, but the rewritten snippet retains it for newly supported recursive paths and now exits on failure. Prefix the operand with ./ or use an absolute path.
findings.evidence: reviewers.md:185 executes readlink -n "${path}" after testing the captured relative path with -L. A standalone system-tool probe, /usr/bin/readlink -n '-vendor/new-link', returned exit 1 with 'illegal option -- v'. The sibling aspect renderer uses ${top_level}/${path}. The option-path fixture contains no symlink, while the documentation-snippet fixture uses module/new-link, so neither covers their combination.
findings.title: Untrusted data in commands: recursive symlink discovery passes option-like paths to readlink
